[ShInternalError](./sh-ast.shinternalerror.md)


</td><td>

Thrown by [parseSync()](./sh-ast.parsesync.md) for failures that should never happen given a correctly-behaving WASM shim: a malformed result envelope, an unexpected root node type, or any other shim contract violation. Distinct from [InputError](./sh-ast.inputerror.md) and [ParseError](./sh-ast.parseerror.md)<!-- -->, both of which indicate a foreseeable, actionable user mistake rather than an internal defect.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ShParseMaxDepthError](./sh-ast.shparsemaxdeptherror.md)


</td><td>

A whole-file parse operation exceeded the binding's native node-nesting budget. The maintained parser counts statement, word, and expression work, including iterative construction of deep operator trees. A refusal returns no partial File or position snapshot and leaves subsequent parse calls available.

This is a binding resource constraint, not an upstream grammar restriction. The fixed 128-unit policy can refuse valid deeply nested input. Units describe native node work, not actual Go/JavaScript frames or necessarily final AST depth. The empirical margin assumes an ordinary caller stack; arbitrary pre-existing JavaScript recursion can exhaust it. This does not establish safety for arbitrary caller-constructed trees or other recursive operations.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[WalkPanicError](./sh-ast.walkpanicerror.md)


</td><td>

A panic raised by upstream-equivalent traversal, such as a nil dereference or unsupported concrete node. Exceptions thrown by callbacks are never wrapped.


</td></tr>

<tr><td>

[parseSync(source, options)](./sh-ast.parsesync.md)


</td><td>

Parses exact source bytes, or well-formed Unicode text encoded as UTF-8. First use synchronously initializes WASM. Native node-nesting work has a fixed binding resource budget; exceeding it throws [ShParseMaxDepthError](./sh-ast.shparsemaxdeptherror.md)<!-- -->. Subsequent parse calls remain usable after that refusal. The returned File and its Node subtrees are plain syntax data: ordinary structuredClone(node), without transfers, makes an independent editable copy while retaining position values, byte strings, typed nils and internal aliases.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[parseWithPositionsSync(source, options)](./sh-ast.parsewithpositionssync.md)


</td><td>

Parses once while observing every real node's upstream bounds in Go. The separate immutable lookup describes this original parse; it never replaces live nodePos/nodeEnd or tracks edits. Source adapters avoid reconstructing each descendant subtree just to display the original source locations.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[printSync(node, options)](./sh-ast.printsync.md)


</td><td>

Formats the current tree with a fresh upstream printer and collects all output. Supported roots are File, Stmt, Word, Assign, Command and WordPart; other Nodes produce PrintError. An ordinary structuredClone of a supported syntax subtree is accepted under the same input and failure rules; copying does not make nil or unsupported roots printable. Only File output has upstream's trailing-newline behavior. Invalid UTF-8 output remains bytes. Upstream formatting can itself consume input bytes, including its tabwriter escape byte, so this is not source replay.

InputError identifies unrepresentable input; PrintError is an ordinary returned upstream error; PrintPanicError retains an upstream operation panic. No partial output or arbitrary writer lifecycle is exposed. Full tree reconstruction and collected output require memory proportional to the values involved; extreme indentation or tree size is not made resource-safe by panic adaptation.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[rawOperator(family, value)](./sh-ast.rawoperator.md)


</td><td>

Represents an unnamed value in an upstream numeric family. Named constants remain precise literal unions; this explicit path preserves other Go values without claiming an operation such as Print accepts them.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[splitBraces(word)](./sh-ast.splitbraces.md)


</td><td>

Applies the selected Go syntax.SplitBraces operation synchronously to a mutable Word and returns its exact boolean. First use initializes WASM synchronously. `true` does not imply that a BraceExp exists: malformed or singleton brace text can return true while being represented again as literals. No fields expand.

The Word keeps its identity. False preserves its Parts array and children; true replaces Parts as Go does, retaining input WordPart objects that Go reuses, including inside new brace elements. Newly split literals retain Go's copied position values; new nodes have no entry in an original PositionSnapshot. Existing aliases to an old Parts array continue to observe that old array.

InputError identifies unrepresentable input. A panic from the selected native operation becomes ShInternalError and leaves the supplied Word unchanged. This operation does not change parser output before explicitly being called.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[walk(node, callback)](./sh-ast.walk.md)


</td><td>

Walks synchronously using the pinned upstream case ordering. Each accepted entry is followed by its children and a null exit. Returning false prunes the entry without an exit; boolean exit return values are ignored. Every callback must return a boolean synchronously; other results produce InputError. Callback exceptions retain their identity, and upstream deferred comment callbacks still run during exception unwinding.

Children and later fields are read live. Each list captures its array reference and length when traversal reaches that list, then reads existing later slots when reached. Replacing or reordering later slots is observed and can cause a node to be skipped or revisited. Indices added beyond the captured extent are not visited by that active list. Replacing the owner's array field does not redirect an active list, but a later walk or print sees the current field. Changes made before a list is reached are observed when it starts.

Supported edits preserve each node's Type (and TypedNil.Kind), required field shapes and every index within each active list's captured extent. Leaving holes or shrinking an array below that extent (for example through truncation, deletion, or length-reducing splice/shift) is outside the mutation contract. These are not runtime validation rules. Ordinary JavaScript object and array aliases remain shared; the binding does not model distinct Go slice headers or capacity-dependent allocation over shared backing storage.

Comments on Stmt, CaseItem and ArrayElem are copied before their callbacks, including position and byte-string values; editing a copy does not edit the stored comment. Last/CondLast/ThenLast/DoLast callbacks receive the stored JavaScript Comment object. Replacing its array slot leaves any previously retained callback object unchanged: there is no Go value-slot pointer identity. Reentrant walks maintain independent traversal state.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<tr><td>

[LangAuto](./sh-ast.langauto.md)


</td><td>

Upstream LangVariant constant LangAuto. Its numeric value is preserved exactly.

LangAuto corresponds to automatic language detection, commonly used by end-user applications like shfmt, which can guess a file's language variant given its filename or shebang.

At this time, `Variant` does not support LangAuto.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[LangBash](./sh-ast.langbash.md)


</td><td>

Upstream LangVariant constant LangBash. Its numeric value is preserved exactly.

LangBash corresponds to the GNU Bash language, as described in its manual at https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html.

We currently follow Bash version 5.2.

Its string representation is "bash".


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[LangBats](./sh-ast.langbats.md)


</td><td>

Upstream LangVariant constant LangBats. Its numeric value is preserved exactly.

LangBats corresponds to the Bash Automated Testing System language, as described at https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core. Note that it's just a small extension of the Bash language.

Its string representation is "bats".


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[LangMirBSDKorn](./sh-ast.langmirbsdkorn.md)


</td><td>

Upstream LangVariant constant LangMirBSDKorn. Its numeric value is preserved exactly.

LangMirBSDKorn corresponds to the MirBSD Korn Shell, also known as mksh, as described at http://www.mirbsd.org/htman/i386/man1/mksh.htm. Note that it shares some features with Bash, due to the shared ancestry that is ksh.

We currently follow mksh version 59.

Its string representation is "mksh".


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[LangPOSIX](./sh-ast.langposix.md)


</td><td>

Upstream LangVariant constant LangPOSIX. Its numeric value is preserved exactly.

LangPOSIX corresponds to the POSIX Shell language, as described at https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/V3\_chap02.html.

Its string representation is "posix" or "sh".


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[LangZsh](./sh-ast.langzsh.md)


</td><td>

Upstream LangVariant constant LangZsh. Its numeric value is preserved exactly.

LangZsh corresponds to the Z shell, as described at https://www.zsh.org/.

Note that its support in the syntax package is experimental and incomplete for now. See https://github.com/mvdan/sh/issues/120.

We currently follow Zsh version 5.9.

Its string representation is "zsh".


</td></tr>
